h: Obelisks, Japanese gardens and an Iron Age fort
p: Kingston Lacy is full of surprises. Out on the lawn stands an ancient Egyptian obelisk brought back from Philae by William John Bankes, an adventurous member of the family who travelled widely in Egypt in the early 1800s. Its inscriptions played a part in the race to decipher hieroglyphs, so it's a real piece of history right there in the Dorset grass.

In the gardens, look out for the Japanese Garden, restored by the National Trust, with its tea house, stone lanterns and calm, carefully planned planting. In late winter, the estate is known for its swathes of snowdrops, which draw visitors in their thousands, and spring brings bluebells to the woods.

Give yourself most of a day here, because the house, gardens and estate walks all add up. Within the wider estate, Badbury Rings is an Iron Age hillfort with grassy ramparts and brilliant views across the countryside. It's a great spot for a breezy walk and a picnic.

Wimborne Minster is just down the road and well worth an afternoon. The minster church has a rare chained library, with old books still fastened to the shelves. The Wimborne Model Town shows the town in miniature, which is fun for younger visitors. The town centre has independent shops, cafés and pubs.
If you're staying in the area, Corfe Castle, the dramatic ruin where the Bankes family lived before Kingston Lacy, is within driving distance to the south, along with the Purbeck coast and beaches.
